rows.title: Slide clearance entered as 12.7 - 0.3 (box 0.6 mm too wide)
rows.why: Ball-bearing slides need >= 12.7 mm per side; 12.4 mm binds or will not engage.

rows.title: Handle c/c 790 on an 800 mm front
rows.why: Handle holes 5 mm from the edge; melamine blows out.

rows.title: 3 mm hardboard as bottom of an 800 mm wide drawer
rows.why: Bottom sags/pops out of the groove under 10-15 kg of clothes.

rows.title: Bottom groove 12 mm deep in an 18.8 mm drawer side
rows.why: Side breaks along the groove.

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer ends E1/E2 1 mm too long
rows.why: Box 1 mm wider than the slides allow: 12.5 mm per side, drawer binds.

rows.title: DXF: contour depth set to 18.5 on 18.8 mm boards
rows.why: Parts are not cut through; prying them out chips the melamine.

rows.title: DXF export dropped one Minifix-bolt hole
rows.why: One joint has no bolt; found during assembly, part must be re-drilled by hand.

rows.title: DXF: one part moved 30 mm into its neighbour
rows.why: Two parts overlap; the router cuts through both.

rows.title: DXF: one part moved 400 mm, off the sheet
rows.why: The part is cut in air/spoilboard; a whole sheet wasted.

rows.title: Gap between nested parts 4 mm with a 6.35 mm bit
rows.why: Neighbouring cuts merge; parts lose their edge and come loose mid-cut.

rows.title: Confirmat 5 mm from top edge of drawer side
rows.why: Screw splits the side.

rows.title: Gap between fronts 0 mm
rows.why: Fronts rub and chip each other.

rows.title: Handle screws M4x30 through 37.6 mm
rows.why: Screw does not reach the handle thread.

rows.title: Generator bug: bottom groove on E1 2 mm higher than on sides
rows.why: Bottom cannot enter all four grooves; box will not close square.

rows.title: Generator bug: Minifix bolt holes in the top forget the overhang
rows.why: Bolts land 21 mm off the side edge holes; top cannot be fitted.

rows.title: Generator bug: side bolt hole for the bottom at y = T instead of T/2
rows.why: Bolt misses the edge hole in the bottom by 9 mm.

rows.title: Plinth strip only 45 mm wide, 1400 mm long
rows.why: Narrow long part shifts under vacuum/hold-down and is ruined.

rows.title: Fronts flush to the bottom (edge 0) -> bottom drawer 1 mm above the carcass bottom
rows.why: Bottom drawer scrapes.

rows.title: 450 mm slide in a 430 mm carcass
rows.why: Slide does not fit.

rows.title: Fronts banded with 2 mm ABS (cut sizes not reduced)
rows.why: Gap between fronts goes from 3 mm to -1 mm; fronts collide.

rows.title: DXF: Minifix housing pocket depth 18.8 (through the board)
rows.why: Housing goes through the visible face.

rows.title: DXF header says inches
rows.why: VCarve imports the job 25.4x too big (or the operator rescales by guess).

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer bottom 4 mm too wide
rows.why: Bottom bottoms out in the groove; box cannot be closed.

rows.title: Regression: right side cut as an identical copy of the left (the bug found on 2026-11-22)
rows.why: Right side: band on the back edge, slide holes 30+ mm too far back; drawer cannot close square.
rows.source: found by R04 on the real kommode

rows.title: Regression: right drawer sides identical to left
rows.why: 8 right drawer sides get slide holes front<->back; slides cannot be mounted.
rows.source: found by R04 on the real kommode

rows.title: Minifix housing depth for 18 mm board drilled in 19 mm board (13.5)
rows.why: Cam sits 0.5 mm proud; bolt head misses the ramp, joint does not pull tight.
rows.source: Häfele TCH 2023 p 7.13

rows.title: Minifix edge bore only 20 mm deep with B24 housing
rows.why: Bolt head stops short of the cam; joint cannot be closed.
rows.source: Häfele TCH 2023 p 7.13/7.18

rows.title: Groove feed 3000 mm/min with 5.6 mm hardboard (groove cut with the 1/8" bit)
rows.why: Above Amana chipload for 1/8"; bit snaps mid-job or burns the groove.
rows.source: Amana compression spiral sheet v12

rows.title: Contour feed 6000 mm/min at 9.5 mm per pass
rows.why: Over Amana 1/4" limit for 1.5xD passes; chipped melamine, deflection, broken bit.
rows.source: Amana compression spiral sheet v12

rows.title: Slide holes typed in from another length (KA 4532/400 with 37/165/357)
rows.why: Rear screw misses the runner hole; runner sits crooked.
rows.source: Hettich MS 10547 p2

rows.title: 1 mm ABS banding on the fronts, cut sizes not reduced
rows.why: Fronts grow 2 mm each way; the 3 mm gap closes to 1 mm and fronts rub.
rows.source: Microvellum KB, cut size = finished - band

rows.title: Onion skin 1.5 mm
rows.why: Parts do not separate; tearing them out chips the melamine face.
rows.source: ShopBot hold-down guide p8

rows.title: Vacuum table only, small drawer parts without tabs
rows.why: Small parts move in the last pass and get gouged.
rows.source: ShopBot hold-down guide p7

rows.title: Slide screws Ø4x10
rows.why: Only 8.8 mm in chipboard; runner pulls out under load.
rows.source: Hettich MS 10547 p1

rows.title: Minifix housing 34 mm from the edge with B24 bolts (24 mm system)
rows.why: Minifix 15 comes in drilling distance B24 and B34; the bolt length is matched to the distance. With the housing 10 mm further in than the bolt reaches, the cam turns past the bolt head and the joint never pulls tight (or the operator over-tightens and cracks the chipboard).
rows.source: Häfele Minifix 15 catalogue / drilling template: housing distance B24 vs B34 must match the bolt type

rows.title: Dowel holes 12 mm (face) + 15 mm (edge) = 27 mm for 8x35 dowels
rows.why: Hole depths must add up to dowel length + ~2 mm glue/air space. With 27 mm the 8x30/8x35 dowel bottoms out and the carcass joint stays open 5-8 mm; Minifix cannot close it either and the edge splits.
rows.source: Dowel joint practice (Häfele/Würth dowel tables, Festool/Wolfcraft dowel jig manuals): face depth + edge depth = dowel length + 1-2 mm; 8 mm dowel in 19 mm board: ~12 face / ~22-25 edge

rows.title: Oak decor board marked "no grain direction" -> nester rotates parts 90°
rows.why: Kaindl oak decor has a printed grain. With rotation allowed the nester turns one side panel 90° on the sheet (653x430 instead of 430x653): the two visible sides get grain in different directions and one must be re-cut from a new oak sheet.
rows.source: Woodworking/nesting practice (VCarve/Cutlist "grain direction lock", panel-saw cutting lists): decor and veneer boards must keep grain orientation

rows.title: Slide screws 20 mm long into 18.8 mm carcass sides
rows.why: Screw goes 18.8 mm into an 18.8 mm side: the tip lifts or pierces the finished OUTER face of the oak side (visible). Hettich/Blum specify 3.5x15/16 chipboard or 6.3x13 Euro screws for side mount slides in 16-19 mm.
rows.source: Hettich KA 4532 / Blum mounting instructions: screw length for side-mount slides in 16-19 mm panels; common forum failure "screw came through the side of the cabinet"

rows.title: Slide hole pattern from the INSET drawing (+19 mm) on an overlay kommode
rows.why: Cabinet member sits 19 mm further back while the drawer member is unchanged: the closed position is 19 mm deeper than the carcass front, so the overlay front hits the carcass edge 19 mm before the slide reaches its stop. Self/soft-close never engages and the drawer springs open.
rows.source: Hettich/Blum slide mounting instructions give separate setback dimensions for overlay vs inset fronts (inset: add front thickness); mixing them is a common cabinet-maker error

rows.title: Edge band added on the top edge of the sides (joint edge) without shortening the part
rows.why: The top sits on the banded edge: sides become 1-2 mm taller than the middle wall, top rocks/gaps, and the Minifix/dowel edge holes are drilled through ABS which chips and misaligns.
rows.source: Edge-banding practice (Homag/Biesse banding guides, cutlist rules): never band edges that are joined; if you must, deduct band thickness from the cut size

rows.title: Slide holes on middle wall 3 mm higher than on the opposite side
rows.why: Each drawer hangs on two slides; if the carcass members are not at the same height the box is twisted, the ball cages bind and the drawer racks or drops off one rail. Hettich/Blum: both runners in one plane, tolerance <=0.5 mm.
rows.source: Hettich KA/Quadro mounting instructions; System 32 line-boring practice

rows.title: Zero gap (fuge) between drawer fronts
rows.why: Fronts touch: edge banding rubs, ABS chips, fronts cannot open past each other and any 0.5 mm swelling or slide sag locks the stack. Overlay fronts need 2-3 mm reveals.
rows.source: Kitchen/overlay front reveal rules (Blum: 2-3 mm gap)

rows.title: Plinth strip placed on top of the leg mounting positions
rows.why: Bunnlist at y=70..89 runs straight through the 40x40 leg plates at y=60..100 near both ends: legs cannot be screwed on, or the strip must be notched by hand.
rows.source: Leg/plinth layout under carcass bottoms (Ikea/Hafele leg plates)

rows.title: Front fixing screws placed exactly on the handle bolt line
rows.why: The 4x30 screw through the drawer end sits where the handle M4 bolt has to pass (front centre, 96 mm off centre): the bolt hits the screw, the handle cannot be fitted.
rows.source: Drawer front attachment practice: keep fixing screws clear of handle bores

rows.title: Bottom groove only 3 mm above lower edge of drawer parts
rows.why: A 3 mm strip of particleboard under a 6.4 mm groove breaks off when the router passes or when the loaded HDF bottom pushes down. Typical minimum 8-12 mm.
rows.source: Drawer box construction (groove 10-12 mm up), particleboard edge strength

rows.title: Groove clearance typed with a minus sign: groove narrower than the HDF
rows.why: Groove 5.6 mm for a 5.9 mm bottom: the bottom cannot be slid in; forcing it splits the groove lips.
rows.source: Sign/typo error in parameters; groove must be board + 0.3-0.5 mm

rows.title: Drawer board thickness measured on the wrong (16 mm) sheet
rows.why: Measured 15.8 on a nominal 19 board: every drawer end is 6 mm too long, boxes are too wide for the slide clearance, grooves and confirmat positions are wrong. A >3 mm deviation is a measurement mix-up, not tolerance.
rows.source: Measuring the wrong offcut/sample; sheet-goods thickness tolerance is +-0.3 mm

rows.title: Dowel only 10 mm from the Minifix bolt
rows.why: Ø8 dowel at 60 next to Ø5 Minifix bolt at 50: 3.5 mm web between bores on the face and on the end edge; the particleboard between them crumbles and neither fitting holds.
rows.source: Hafele/Hettich connector spacing: keep >=32 mm (System 32) between connector and dowel

rows.title: Oak decor grain flag lost: fronts/top/sides nested rotated
rows.why: Kaindl Eik Dew has a grain direction; with retning=False the nester rotates parts freely - here the right side CH is nested turned 90 deg, so its grain runs vertically while the left side runs horizontally. Visible on the finished piece, cannot be fixed after cutting.
rows.source: Decor/veneer grain direction in nesting software (grain lock)

rows.title: Side panel slide holes referenced from the back edge
rows.why: Slide pilots on the left side C at DEP-x instead of x from the front (C now looks like the mirrored CH): the left runners sit ~36 mm further back than the middle-wall runners, the drawer cannot be mounted square and the front will not close flush.
rows.source: Wrong reference edge / origin in CNC programs (front-edge reference for slides)

rows.title: Drawer-side slide holes 12 mm too low on the box
rows.why: Box-member holes on the left drawer sides (S) are 12 mm off the box centre while the right sides (SH) are correct: every box hangs tilted, the bottom drawer drags on the carcass bottom and fronts are skewed.
rows.source: Box-member mounting height vs cabinet-member height (Hettich/Blum)

rows.title: Top dowel/Minifix holes miss the front overhang offset
rows.why: Holes in the top ignore the 21 mm overhang: the top sits flush with the carcass front, so the 18.8 mm drawer fronts stand proud of the top and the top hangs 24 mm over the back.
rows.source: Offset/reference error between mating parts (top vs side edge bores)

rows.title: Minifix cam housings in the bottom at 34 mm instead of 24 mm
rows.why: The cam must sit at the bolt-head distance (24 mm for this bolt). At 34 mm the bolt head does not reach the cam: no clamping, the carcass joint is loose.
rows.source: Hafele Minifix 15 drilling data (dimension B = 24 mm)

rows.title: Middle wall cut full side height (bottom thickness not subtracted)
rows.why: Middle wall stands on the bottom but is cut 653 mm: 18.8 mm too tall, the top cannot come down onto the sides and all Minifix joints at the top stay open.
rows.source: Classic carcass arithmetic error (forgot one board thickness)

rows.title: Drawer bottom 2 mm too large in both directions
rows.why: Bottom is 1 mm per side deeper than the groove bottoms: the box cannot be closed, or is forced out of square / bows the sides.
rows.source: Panel-in-groove sizing (groove depth minus play)

rows.title: Drawer box 2 mm too wide for the slides
rows.why: Ends/bottom 2 mm long: 1 mm less than the 12.7 mm slide clearance per side. Ball-bearing slides tolerate +-0.2 mm; the drawer jams or the slide must be forced.
rows.source: Hettich KA 4532 / Accuride: side clearance 12.7 +0.2/-0

rows.title: Only 7 drawer fronts generated for 8 drawers
rows.why: Off-by-one in quantity: cut list and sheets both say 7, one drawer has no front. Found at assembly, a second oak sheet run for one part.
rows.source: Off-by-one quantity bugs in cut lists

rows.title: Sheet exported in inches but header still says mm
rows.why: All coordinates on the drawer-parts sheet are 25.4x too small while $INSUNITS=4 (mm). The CAM imports tiny parts; if scaled by guess, everything is off.
rows.source: DXF unit mismatch (VCarve/ShopBot import scale)

rows.title: Minifix housing pockets drilled through the oak sides
rows.why: Layer depth for Ø15 cam housings written as Z18.8 (full thickness) instead of Z13.5: Ø15 holes through the visible outside of both side panels.
rows.source: Layer-encoded depth errors in CAM templates

rows.title: Contour depth set for 16 mm board on 18.8 mm sheet
rows.why: Profile depth Z16 leaves 2.8 mm uncut: parts are not freed, have to be broken/cut out by hand, edges chip and the parts may shift during later ops.
rows.source: Reusing a toolpath template from a thinner material

rows.title: One drawer back (E2) missing from its sheet
rows.why: Sheet has 7 E2 while the cut list says 8: one box has no back, second machine run.
rows.source: Part count on sheet vs cut list mismatch (manual nest edit)

rows.title: Part placed beyond the sheet edge
rows.why: The rightmost part on the oak sheet extends 40 mm past the 2440 mm sheet: the bit cuts air or the clamps/bed, part comes out short.
rows.source: Manual nest edits / bed size mismatch

rows.title: Oak sheet exported mirrored (Y flipped)
rows.why: All hole patterns are mirrored inside their parts (origin top-left vs bottom-left): top dowels at the wrong distance from the front, slide holes top/bottom swapped on the sides.
rows.source: Mirror/flip on DXF export or wrong CAM origin corner

rows.title: Blind holes exported with radius = diameter
rows.why: Circles on 01_BOR layers are twice the size: Ø5 Minifix bolt bores become Ø10, Ø8 dowels Ø16 - nothing holds, and the CAM may pocket them.
rows.source: Radius/diameter confusion in DXF writers

rows.title: Labels swapped between a front end (E1) and a back end (E2)
rows.why: The part labelled E1 has no front fixing holes and the one labelled E2 has them: built into the wrong position, the front cannot be screwed on.
rows.source: Mislabelled parts on nested sheets

rows.title: Drawer box height typed from the front height: box taller than the row pitch
rows.why: Each drawer box is taller than the distance between slide rows, so the boxes of neighbouring rows collide; the drawers cannot be installed together and the cut drawer sides/ends are scrap.
rows.source: designer typed front height (+ clearance) into the box-height field

rows.title: Top overhang entered with a minus sign: top shallower than the carcass
rows.why: The top is cut ~40 mm short in depth, so it stops 21 mm behind the front edge of the sides and does not cover the back panel; the oak top is scrap and the carcass cannot be finished.
rows.source: sign error on an offset field (overhang vs setback)

rows.title: Drawer boxes assigned to 6 mm hardboard instead of 19 mm chipboard
rows.why: Drawer sides/ends come out of 5.9 mm hardboard: 8 mm bottom grooves cut through, Ø7 confirmat screws cannot hold in 6 mm board and the slides cannot be screwed on. All drawer boxes are scrap.
rows.source: wrong material picked from the drop-down for one role

rows.title: Sheet edge margin set to 0 mm
rows.why: Parts are nested right up to the raw sheet edge where the hold-down clamps/screws are; the bit runs into the clamps (broken bit, possible projectile) and the chipped factory edge ends up on visible parts.
rows.source: nesting margin zeroed to squeeze one more part on the sheet

rows.title: 1/8" bit flute length entered as 38 mm (overall length)
rows.why: Small through holes are no longer spot-drilled: the CNC plunges a 3.175 mm bit with a 12.7 mm flute through 18.8 mm board, the shank burns in and the bit snaps.
rows.source: tool table: overall length typed in the cutting-length field

rows.title: Plinth strip taller than the legs
rows.why: The plinth strips hang 12 mm below the feet, so the kommode stands on the strips, rocks, and the legs never touch the floor; the strips (and screw holes in the bottom) must be remade.
rows.source: plinth height chosen without checking the leg height

rows.title: Drawer bottom play per side typed as 9 mm (meant 0.9)
rows.why: The bottom is smaller than the span between the groove bottoms minus the groove depth, so it does not engage the grooves at all and drops out of every drawer.
rows.source: missing decimal point in a clearance field

rows.title: Slide pilot hole diameter set to 6 mm for Ø4 screws
rows.why: The slide pilot holes are larger than the Ø4 slide screws; the screws spin freely, the slides cannot be fixed and every side, middle wall and drawer side is drilled wrong.
rows.source: screw head/washer diameter typed as pilot diameter

rows.title: Drawer centre offset over front centre typed -70 (meant -7)
rows.why: Drawer boxes and slides move 70 mm down: the bottom drawer box/slide sits below the carcass bottom and every slide row is misaligned with its front, so no drawer can be mounted.
rows.source: missing decimal point / unit slip in an offset field

rows.title: Generator bug: handle hole x/y swapped on the fronts
rows.why: Handle holes are placed at y = 304/496 on a 160 mm high front, i.e. off the part; the CNC drills into the neighbouring part or spoilboard and the fronts get no (correct) handle holes.
rows.source: axis swap in a coordinate transform

rows.title: Generator bug: right side CH mirrored top-bottom instead of front-back
rows.why: The right side gets its slide holes and joint holes flipped vertically: the right slides sit at different heights from the left ones and the Minifix housings land at the bottom. The oak side is scrap.
rows.source: mirror about the wrong axis when deriving the handed part

rows.title: Generator bug: middle wall uses the same slide hole pattern on both faces
rows.why: The left-face slide holes are drilled at the same x as the right-face ones, so 12.8 mm screws from both sides meet in an 18.8 mm wall; the screws collide/split the wall and one side of slides cannot be fixed.
rows.source: alternate hole pattern for the opposite face ignored

rows.title: Generator bug: mirrored right drawer side SH has no bottom groove
rows.why: Right drawer sides are cut without the groove for the drawer bottom, so the bottom cannot be slid in and the drawers cannot be assembled.
rows.source: operation dropped when copying/mirroring a part

rows.title: Generator bug: plinth screw holes in the bottom offset by one board thickness
rows.why: The holes for the plinth screws land beside the plinth strips instead of over their centre line; screws go into air and the plinth cannot be fixed.
rows.source: reference edge vs centre-line mix-up for mating hole pattern

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer front width ignores the number of columns
rows.why: Every drawer front is cut the full width of the kommode instead of half; fronts overlap each other, handle holes are off-centre, and 8 oak fronts are scrap.
rows.source: division by column count lost in a refactor

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer bottoms nested on the 19 mm drawer-side board
rows.why: The drawer bottoms are cut out of 18.8 mm chipboard instead of 6 mm hardboard; they cannot enter the 6.4 mm grooves, and the shared sheet gets the wrong contour depth for one of the thicknesses.
rows.source: material/role mapping bug in the part list

rows.title: Generator bug: top joint holes placed on the visible upper face
rows.why: Minifix bolt and dowel holes are specified on the oak top's show face instead of the underside; they are drilled into the visible surface and the top is ruined.
rows.source: face flag (F1/F2) inverted for one part

rows.title: DXF: contour polylines exported open (closed flag cleared)
rows.why: CAM treats the outlines as open chains: no inside/outside offset can be applied, the last edge is not cut, and parts are either cut on the line (undersize) or not released.
rows.source: DXF exporter writes POLYLINE flag 70=0 instead of 1

rows.title: DXF: contours on one sheet exported on layer "0"
rows.why: The CAM template maps tools and depths by layer; the outlines on layer 0 get no profile toolpath (or a default engrave), so the sheet is drilled but the parts are never cut out, or cut at the wrong depth.
rows.source: layer names dropped on export (everything to layer 0)

rows.title: DXF: part labels exported on the contour layer
rows.why: The label text is on the through-cut layer, so the CNC routes the letters full depth into the faces of every part on that sheet: parts ruined.
rows.source: text entities assigned to the wrong layer

rows.title: DXF: bottom grooves drawn across the part instead of along it
rows.why: The groove rectangles are rotated 90 degrees: the 8 mm deep groove runs across the drawer parts and into their neighbours, cutting them in two.
rows.source: groove not rotated together with a rotated part in the nester

rows.title: DXF: Minifix housing circles exported on a Ø5 drill layer
rows.why: The CAM drills the 15 mm housings with a 5 mm drill cycle at the centre; the Minifix cams do not fit and the carcass cannot be assembled.
rows.source: layer mapping: pocket circles assigned to a drill layer

rows.title: DXF: outer contours on one sheet exported as inside contours
rows.why: Tool compensation goes to the inside of the line, so every part on the sheet comes out one bit diameter (6.35 mm) too small in both directions.
rows.source: wrong layer suffix/tool-side in the export template

rows.title: DXF: largest contour on a sheet has two vertices swapped (bow-tie)
rows.why: The outline self-intersects; CAM cannot offset it, or cuts a diagonal straight through the part.
rows.source: vertex order corrupted on export

rows.title: DXF: two same-size sheet files for different boards have swapped contents
rows.why: The operator loads the oak sheet and cuts the white carcass parts on it (and vice versa): wrong decor on fronts/sides and both sheets wasted.
rows.source: file names and contents mixed up when exporting/uploading per material

rows.title: Handle hole diameter typed as 3 mm for M4 handle bolts
rows.why: The M4 handle bolts do not pass through the Ø3 holes in the fronts; drilling them out by hand on the finished oak fronts chips the decor and the handles end up crooked.
rows.source: Hardware fit: thread size confused with tap-drill size

rows.title: Minifix bolt pilot holes set to Ø8 (dowel size) instead of Ø5
rows.why: The screw-in Minifix bolts have nothing to bite into in an Ø8 hole, so the carcass joints to the top, bottom and middle wall cannot be tightened; every joint hole is wrong.
rows.source: Joinery: dowel diameter copied into the Minifix bolt field

rows.title: Slide pilot depth set to 18 mm in 18.8 mm sides
rows.why: Slide pilot holes go (almost) through the side panels and blow out on the visible oak outside face of the carcass at every slide screw.
rows.source: Tooling: blind-hole depth entered as board thickness

rows.title: Machine bed entered as 2500x1250 (sheet-ish size) instead of the router's 2440x1220
rows.why: The dealer saws pieces bigger than the ShopBot bed and the nest uses the extra 60/30 mm: parts at the far end cannot be reached or clamped, the job overruns the machine limits.
rows.source: Nesting/sheet: machine envelope taken from a quote instead of the workshop

rows.title: Rear leg positions 100 mm deeper than the carcass
rows.why: The rear legs are marked outside the bottom panel: they hang off the back, cannot be screwed to the bottom and the chest rocks/tips backwards.
rows.source: Assembly/safety: leg y measured from the top front edge instead of the carcass front

rows.title: Side height typed 1653 instead of 653
rows.why: A 1.65 m tall, 43 cm deep chest of drawers with only four drawers: sides and back are cut far too long and the finished piece is a tip-over hazard.
rows.source: Geometry: extra digit in an outer dimension

rows.title: Adjustable front-fixing holes in the drawer front ends set to Ø14
rows.why: The 4x30 screws and their washers pull straight through the Ø14 holes, so the fronts cannot be fastened to the drawer boxes.
rows.source: Hardware fit: washer diameter typed as the slot/hole size

rows.title: Minifix/joint positions set 8 mm from the front and back edges
rows.why: Ø15 cam housings and bolt holes break out of the front edge of the sides/middle wall, the edge bores split the chipboard and the joints have no strength.
rows.source: Joinery: edge distance from a 16 mm system drawing misread

rows.title: Drawer-bottom HDF thickness typed 59 instead of 5.9
rows.why: The bottom groove becomes ~60 mm wide on 120 mm drawer parts: it eats half the drawer side, crosses the confirmat holes and the box falls apart.
rows.source: Materials: decimal point lost when entering a measured thickness

rows.title: Generator bug: back panel height taken from carcass depth (430) instead of side height
rows.why: The back panel is cut 430 mm high on a 653 mm carcass: the back is open, the carcass is not squared and the panel sheet is wasted.
rows.source: Generator: wrong variable for one dimension

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer sides cut to carcass depth instead of slide length
rows.why: Drawer sides become 430 mm while ends, bottoms and slides are for 400: the bottom no longer reaches the back groove, the box hits the back panel and drawers do not close.
rows.source: Drawer mechanics: slide length vs carcass depth confusion

rows.title: Generator bug: confirmat holes in drawer sides offset to the inner face of the end boards
rows.why: The 7 mm confirmat holes sit on the joint line instead of the centre of the 18.8 mm end: screws split out of the end grain and the drawer boxes cannot be assembled.
rows.source: Joinery: hole at board thickness instead of half thickness

rows.title: Generator bug: only one handle hole on every drawer front
rows.why: Two-bolt bar handles cannot be fitted; drilling the second hole by hand on finished oak fronts gives misaligned handles across all eight drawers.
rows.source: Hardware: list-index bug drops the last op

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer bottom length and width swapped
rows.why: Bottoms are cut 377 x 725 instead of 725 x 377: they cannot go into the drawer box grooves at all, all eight bottoms are scrap.
rows.source: Geometry: L/B transposed for one part

rows.title: Generator bug: front-fixing screw holes drilled in the back end (E2) instead of the front end (E1)
rows.why: There is no way to screw the fronts to the drawer boxes from inside; the holes in the back ends are useless.
rows.source: Assembly: ops attached to the wrong part

rows.title: Generator bug: side Minifix housings for the top drawn at the bottom end of the sides
rows.why: The top-edge bolts in the sides have no cam housing to engage, the top cannot be locked down and there are stray Ø15 pockets near the bottom joint.
rows.source: Joinery: y measured from the wrong reference edge

rows.title: Generator bug: bottom groove width from drawer-side thickness instead of HDF thickness
rows.why: Grooves are ~19 mm wide for a 6 mm bottom: the bottom rattles, the groove runs into the confirmat holes and the lower edge of the drawer parts breaks off.
rows.source: Drawer mechanics: wrong thickness variable for a groove

rows.title: DXF: one sheet exported with its origin at the sheet centre
rows.why: All coordinates are shifted by half a sheet into negative X/Y: with zero at the sheet corner the router runs off the sheet into clamps/limits and cuts the parts in the wrong places.
rows.source: File format: drawing origin vs machine zero

rows.title: DXF: holes of one part left in part-local coordinates (not moved with the part)
rows.why: The holes of one part are drilled near the sheet origin, through a neighbouring part or the margin, while the part itself is cut without its holes.
rows.source: Export: block explode / transform not applied to child entities

rows.title: DXF: Minifix housing pockets shifted 8 mm on one sheet
rows.why: The cam housings no longer line up with the edge-bored bolts, so the cams cannot catch the bolts and the carcass joints do not close.
rows.source: Export: pocket layer offset (tool-compensation / layer offset applied twice)

rows.title: DXF: bottom-groove rectangles exported on the outer-contour layer
rows.why: The CAM profiles every groove full depth: all drawer sides and ends are sliced into strips.
rows.source: Layers: wrong layer mapping in the export

rows.title: DXF: sheet file truncated during transfer (last ~45% of entities and EOF missing)
rows.why: Depending on the CAM, the import fails or silently loads only half of the parts/holes; the sheet is cut incomplete and the missing parts are discovered at assembly.
rows.source: File transfer: USB stick pulled / upload interrupted

rows.title: DXF: decimal marker lost in contour-layer depth (Z18P8 -> Z188)
rows.why: CAM layer mapping reads a 188 mm cut depth: the bit plunges through the sheet and spoilboard into the table, breaking the bit.
rows.source: File format: layer-name encoding of depth corrupted

rows.title: DXF: one part's contour exported rotated 90 deg while its holes are not
rows.why: The part is cut to the wrong outline: its holes and grooves fall outside it and it cuts across its neighbours on the sheet.
rows.source: Export: rotation applied to the outline but not to the machining

rows.title: DXF: slide pilot-hole layer frozen at export (all Ø3.175 pilots missing on one sheet)
rows.why: The slide mounting holes are not drilled: slides must be positioned by hand, drawers end up crooked and the fronts do not line up.
rows.source: Layers: frozen/off layer not exported

rows.title: Dealer saw kerf entered as 0 mm (plater.sagsnitt)
rows.why: The panel saw removes ~4 mm per cut, but the offcut pieces are nested as if no material is lost: the second piece is drawn 4 mm larger than the real offcut, so parts nested at its far edge run off the board and are ruined.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; panel-saw kerf is always 3-4.5 mm

rows.title: Front edge reveal (kant_topp_bunn) typed negative
rows.why: Front stack becomes taller than the carcass: the top drawer front runs up into the top overhang and cannot close, the bottom one hangs below the carcass - all 8 oak fronts recut.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; sign error when entering an overlay "overhang" instead of a reveal

rows.title: Front-fixing screw holes in E1 copied from the confirmat layout (on the confirmat bore)
rows.why: The 4x30 front screws are drilled straight across the 5 mm confirmat pilot in the end grain of the front end: the confirmat and the screw collide, the end board splits and the front cannot be fixed.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; positions reused from the wrong hole table

rows.title: Drawer side height lower than the slide (low-drawer option with a 46 mm slide)
rows.why: The slide body is taller than the drawer side: its screws run off the side, slide pilot holes break out of the edges and the drawer cannot be mounted.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; wrong row from the slide catalogue

rows.title: Rear plinth strip position entered for its back face (flush-intent), generator uses the front face
rows.why: Strip sticks out behind the carcass back so the chest cannot stand against the wall, and its screw holes break out of the bottom panel back edge.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; reference-face confusion

rows.title: Top front overhang typed 10x too large (e.g. 210 instead of 21)
rows.why: A deep unsupported top far in front of the front legs: leaning on it or a child climbing opened drawers tips the chest forward (tip-over hazard), and a big oak part is wasted.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; decimal slip; furniture tip-over injuries (EN 14749 / ASTM F2057)

rows.title: Drawer bottom groove raised to half the box height (groove on the slide screw line)
rows.why: The groove runs exactly where the slide pilots go: slide screws end in the empty groove with no grip and the drawer side is weakened along the line carrying the load - drawers drop out under weight.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; "hidden bottom" tweak without checking the hardware

rows.title: Carcass depth typed as the slide length (430 -> 400)
rows.why: The slide needs more inside depth than its nominal length: drawers will not close fully against the back panel and the slide rear brackets clash with it - sides, bottom, top, middle wall all wrong depth.
rows.source: Designer input error (params.json), workshop experience; slide minimum inside depth (Hettich KA spec)

rows.title: Generator bug: spot-drill fallback lost - small-bit through holes sent as full-depth through cuts
rows.why: Holes smaller than the big bit (handle, slide pilots, plinth screws) are plunged through 18.8 mm with the 1/8" bit whose flute is only 12.7 mm: shank rubs, bit overheats and snaps, burned holes.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build()); flute length vs. stock thickness, small-bit breakage

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer bottom quantity = rows instead of rows x columns
rows.why: Only half the drawer bottoms are cut: four drawers cannot be assembled, a second HDF job (and maybe sheet) needed.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build())

rows.title: Generator bug: middle wall quantity 0 (cols - 2)
rows.why: No middle wall is cut: the inner slides of both columns have nothing to mount on and the top/bottom holes for it lead nowhere - carcass cannot be assembled.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build()); off-by-one in a count

rows.title: Generator bug: back drawer end E2 has no bottom groove
rows.why: The drawer bottom is sized to sit in grooves on all four sides; with no groove in the back end it hits E2 and the box cannot be closed - 8 back ends recut.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build())

rows.title: Generator bug: top cut to the inner width (between the sides) instead of the full width
rows.why: The top no longer covers the sides and its bolt/dowel holes for the sides fall off the part: wasted oak top.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build()); length copied from the bottom panel formula

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer fronts assigned to the white carcass board instead of the oak front board
rows.why: All 8 fronts are nested and cut from white melamine: wrong finish, sheets wasted, oak sheet half empty.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build()); wrong material role

rows.title: Generator bug: top holes for the middle wall use the bottom panel coordinates (offset one board thickness)
rows.why: The top is measured from the outer edge but the bottom from inside the side: middle-wall bolt and dowel holes in the top miss the wall by ~19 mm, the wall stands crooked or cannot be joined.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build()); wrong coordinate reference

rows.title: Generator bug: bottom panel edge bores for the side Minifix bolts dropped
rows.why: Nothing for the cam bolts to enter: the bottom is held to the sides only by dowels and the carcass racks or falls apart when moved.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build())

rows.title: Generator bug: grooves in the drawer ends half as deep as the bottom is sized for
rows.why: Bottom is long enough for the full groove depth but E1/E2 grooves are shallow: the drawer box will not close by several mm, glue/confirmats pull the joints open.
rows.source: Generator regression (kommode.py build())

rows.title: DXF: groove layer on the first drawer sheet exported with the full board (contour) depth
rows.why: The bottom groove is cut right through the drawer sides/ends: every part on the sheet splits along the groove line and the whole sheet is scrap.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; depth copied from the contour layer when the CAM layer map was built

rows.title: DXF: drawer-bottom HDF sheet exported empty (only the sheet outline)
rows.why: The operator runs the job, nothing is cut: all 8 drawer bottoms missing at assembly time.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF

rows.title: DXF: slide pilot holes on the oak sheet exported on a through-hole layer
rows.why: Blind slide pilots are drilled through the oak sides: rows of holes on the visible outside of the chest.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; layer mapping error

rows.title: DXF: bottom grooves overrun 40 mm past the part ends
rows.why: Grooves run out through the 10 mm gap into neighbouring parts: every neighbour gets a groove scar and is scrap.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; lead-in/lead-out added on the geometry instead of in CAM

rows.title: DXF: tool compensation applied twice - contours on the front sheet offset inward by a bit diameter
rows.why: CAM offsets again for the bit, so every front comes out one bit diameter too small each way: gaps everywhere, handle holes off-centre - all fronts recut.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; double cutter compensation (CAM + exporter)

rows.title: DXF: one corner of the largest contour moved 5 mm (part out of square)
rows.why: Biggest part comes out as a trapezoid: carcass racks, gaps and joints do not close.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; edited/snapped vertex in CAD

rows.title: DXF: confirmat through-holes drawn with the Ø10 countersink circle on the Ø7 layer
rows.why: Geometry and layer disagree; CAM follows the circle and cuts Ø10 holes, the confirmat heads pull straight through the drawer sides.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF

rows.title: DXF: part labels stripped from the drawer-box sheets
rows.why: Mirrored S/SH sides and E1/E2 ends are indistinguishable: wrong-handed sides go together, slide holes face inward, front-fixing holes end up at the back.
rows.source: CAM/export/transfer error on the sheet DXF; text entities dropped by an export filter

rows.title: Front leg positions measured from the back edge: all four legs in the rear half
rows.why: bein_senter y for the front legs entered from the back. All legs end up near the back, the whole drawer load is cantilevered in front of the support line - the kommode tips forward when a loaded drawer is opened.
rows.source: CPSC / ASTM F2057 furniture tip-over: support base vs. drawer extension; leg placement drawings

rows.title: Top + sides switched to a thinner (16 mm) board in materialvalg while carcass stays 19 mm
rows.why: The outer parts are still sized, drilled and contoured for the 18.8 mm carcass thickness, but the sheet is 16 mm: contours plunge ~3 mm into the spoilboard, Minifix bolts/housings no longer meet, carcass is out of square.
rows.source: Workshop: substituting a cheaper/thinner board at order time without re-running the joint layout

rows.title: Dealer offcut minimum typed 1500 instead of 150 mm (plater.min_bit)
rows.why: Every saw-split piece under 1.5 m is dropped, so the 846 mm strip of each 2800x2070 sheet is thrown away and the nest needs extra whole sheets - wasted oak and an order that does not match the cut plan.
rows.source: Panel-saw splitting at the dealer; extra zero typed in a parameter file

rows.title: Plinth inset from the ends typed 810 instead of 81 mm (strip length negative)
rows.why: bunnlist_inn_fra_ende x10: the plinth length LB - 2*inset becomes negative/impossible and the screw holes in the bottom land outside any strip - nothing can be cut or assembled under the bottom.
rows.source: Extra digit in a parametric input; plinth sizing

rows.title: Bottom groove programmed in a single pass (maskintid.omganger_not = 1)
rows.why: The full 8 mm deep groove is cut in one pass with the 1/8" bit (groove < 6.35 mm) - 2.5x the bit diameter in one go snaps the small bit and burns the melamine.
rows.source: Router-bit makers: max depth of cut per pass ~1x diameter for 1/8" bits in particle board

rows.title: Lower confirmat height set on the bottom-groove line
rows.why: konfirmat_y[0] placed at the centre of the bottom groove: the 7 mm confirmat hole goes through the groove, the screw lands in the HDF slot, the joint has nothing to bite into and the groove edge blows out.
rows.source: Drawer box joinery: fasteners must clear the bottom groove

rows.title: Front-fixing screw heights laid out on the 160 mm front instead of the 120 mm drawer end
rows.why: front_skrue_y taken from the front height: the upper fixing holes fall at or beyond the top edge of the E1 drawer end - holes break out of the part, front cannot be screwed on.
rows.source: Measuring from the wrong drawing (front vs. box end)

rows.title: Minifix housing diameter set to 35 mm (hinge-cup Forstner size)
rows.why: minifix_hus_d 35 instead of 15: the pocket is far wider than the cam, the 24 mm housing distance puts the pocket over the board edge - edges blow out and the cam has no wall to pull against.
rows.source: Hettich/Häfele: Minifix 15 housing Ø15; Ø35 is the concealed-hinge cup bit

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer sides shortened by two end-board thicknesses
rows.why: S/SH cut to Ls - 2*ts as if the ends were butted outside the sides: the box is 37.6 mm shorter than the slide, the drawer ends no longer reach the bottom grooves of the sides and the slide overhangs the box.
rows.source: Classic butt-joint formula error (end thickness subtracted on the wrong part)

rows.title: Generator bug: middle wall cut to the top depth (front overhang + back panel included)
rows.why: D length taken from the top (OV + DEP + back): the wall sticks out in front of the carcass and hits the drawer fronts; at the back it collides with the back panel - fronts cannot close.
rows.source: Copying the wrong reference dimension between parts

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer-end front-fixing holes also drilled through the oak fronts
rows.why: The E1 Ø8 through-hole pattern is appended to the K fronts: four visible holes through every one of the 8 oak fronts - all fronts scrapped.
rows.source: Shared op list reused between mating parts

rows.title: Generator bug: confirmat end-grain pilots in E1/E2 at full screw diameter (Ø7 instead of Ø5)
rows.why: The pilot in the end grain equals the confirmat shank: the thread has nothing to cut into chipboard end grain, screws spin out and the drawer box falls apart.
rows.source: Confirmat 7x50: clearance Ø7 in the face, pilot Ø5 in the end grain (Häfele)

rows.title: Generator bug: confirmat end-grain pilots of E1/E2 emitted as through-holes in the face
rows.why: Edge ops converted to CNC through-holes at the part ends: holes through the face of every drawer end, small bit plunged through 18.8 mm, and the end grain has no pilot for the screw.
rows.source: Edge vs. face op confusion in a CAM post

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer-side slide pilots cut 10 mm blind from the inner face
rows.why: Slide screws enter from the outside of S/SH, but the pilots are blind holes from the inside face: the outer face has no hole and the blind hole breaks the 2.8 mm skin - slides cannot be fixed accurately.
rows.source: Side-mount slide installation (screw face vs. machined face)

rows.title: Generator bug: back panel height includes the top thickness
rows.why: G cut HS + T tall: it stands 18.8 mm proud of the sides into the zone the top covers - the top cannot sit down on the carcass, joints gape.
rows.source: Back panel captured under the top vs. on top of the sides

rows.title: Generator bug: drawer-bottom groove also cut into the carcass sides
rows.why: The groove op is appended to C and CH: a 6.4 mm slot runs the full depth of both oak sides, visible at the front edge and through the Minifix bolt holes - both sides scrapped.
rows.source: Shared op dict leaking between part builders

rows.title: Generator bug: middle-wall Minifix housings drilled on both faces
rows.why: Housings 14 mm deep from F1 and again from F2 at the same spots in an 18.8 mm wall: they meet, leaving holes through the wall and no material for the cams.
rows.source: Double-sided part with mirrored op list applied twice

rows.title: DXF: sheet reference outline exported on the outer-contour layer
rows.why: The 00_PLATE_REFERANSE rectangle lands on the contour layer: CAM profiles the sheet border at full depth, running the bit into clamps/screws at the sheet edge - broken bit, unsafe.
rows.source: Layer mapping errors in CAM import

rows.title: DXF: groove layer width and depth swapped (B6P4_Z8 -> B8_Z6P4)
rows.why: The groove is cut 8 mm wide and 6.4 mm deep: the HDF bottom rattles in the slot and is sized for a deeper groove, so it does not fit between the drawer parts.
rows.source: Layer-name template fields swapped in the exporter

rows.title: DXF: bulge values on contour vertices (straight edges exported as arcs)
rows.why: Group 42 bulge set on every vertex of one sheet: the CAM cuts each edge as an arc - parts bow in/out by several mm over their length and nothing fits.
rows.source: Polyline bulge left over from a fillet/offset operation

rows.title: DXF: stray vertex at the origin inserted into the largest contour
rows.why: An uninitialised (0,0) vertex in a contour: the toolpath jumps diagonally across the sheet at full depth, cutting through the neighbouring parts.
rows.source: Exporter emits default-initialised vertex

rows.title: DXF: two sheets of the same board written into one file
rows.why: The parts of the second sheet are appended to the first: overlapping contours and holes on one sheet - the cut destroys both sets of parts.
rows.source: Export loop not resetting the entity buffer between sheets

rows.title: DXF: bottom grooves stop 25 mm short of the part ends
rows.why: Grooves no longer run out at the ends: the HDF bottom cannot reach under the end boards, the box cannot be closed, and stopped grooves leave rounded ends.
rows.source: Lead-in/lead-out trimmed into the geometry

rows.title: DXF: largest through-hole layer exported as a 5 mm blind drill
rows.why: Through holes (confirmat/front-fixing) on one sheet become 5 mm deep blind holes: screws cannot pass, every hole must be re-drilled by hand and will wander.
rows.source: CAM layer template mapping GJENNOM to a fixed drill depth

rows.title: DXF: contour vertices on one sheet exported at Z = -board thickness
rows.why: Elevation added to the vertices: CAM that uses geometry Z adds it to the layer depth and cuts twice the board thickness deep - into the spoilboard/bed, bit overloaded.
rows.source: 3D-polyline elevation leaking into a 2D export

3 columns, 1800 wide
1 column, 820 wide, 100 mm boxes

Thin boards measured (18.4 / 5.6)
